text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Around 14,000 support staff will be recruited for schools nationwide to ease the administrative burden of teachers, Education Minster Najib Tun Razak said on Monday.

-- Malaysia's five-day Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC) promotional tour to the U.S. which began on Monday aims to educate Americans on the aims of the project. The MSC is a 15-by-50 kilometre zone south of Kuala Lumpur which is slated to be an information technology backbone for the country.

-- A director of Malaysian motor distributor UMW Holdings Bhd urged the government not to sell its stake in the company to telecommunications company Sapura Holdings Sdn Bhd, as it was among the "top five investments" of the state-run pension fund.

-- Ailing national steel maker Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd is confident of doing better, following the government's decision to absorb the company's 2.9 billion ringgit debt, said executive committee chairman Abu Sahid Mohamed on Monday.
-- Direct seller Amway (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd expects sales growth of 49.6 percent for the first quarter of 1997 compared to the same period in 1996.
-- Segari Energy ventures, a unit of Malakoff Holdings Bhd, is ready to supply power to national power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd, said Malakoff managing director Ahmad Jauhari Yahya on Monday.
